extracted.intended_audience: federal agency rulewriters, regulatory drafters, and agency guidance-policy officials
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for agency drafters on how to draft and present contemporaneous guidance in preambles to final rules (organization, content, limits, presentation, and integration with other guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of basis and purpose should address statutory objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: In the statement of basis and purpose accompanying a final rule, agencies should address how the rule advances statutory objectives. Such discussion should go beyond merely repeating the text or title of the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preambles must meaningfully explain how the rule furthers the statute's goals rather than restating statutory language; omission reduces usefulness and can violate the APA requirement to accompany a final rule with a statement of the rule's 'basis and purpose.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Include section-by-section analysis for lengthy regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consider including, particularly for lengthy regulations, a section-by-section analysis in the preamble in which the organization of the preambular discussion corresponds to the organization of the final rules themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section-by-section analyses should go beyond merely repeating the regulatory text discussed. Organizing preambles to mirror the rule structure aids findability and helps readers map explanation to regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid scattering basis/purpose across multiple documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When agencies incorporate or rely upon discussions of a rule's basis and purpose from prior notices, such as from the notice of proposed rulemaking, they should be mindful that such incorporation and reliance may make it more burdensome for readers to find all relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not force readers to integrate multiple agency documents to discover the full basis and purpose; either consolidate key explanatory material in the final rule preamble or provide clear cross-references and links to the prior material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use preamble as a substitute for regulatory text; avoid mandatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should not use the preamble as a substitute for regulatory language. Agencies should avoid use of mandatory language in the preambles to final rules, unless an agency is using these words to describe a statutory, regulatory, or constitutional requirement, or the language is addressed to agency staff and will not foreclose agency consideration of positions advanced by affected parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory terms to avoid in preambles include 'shall,' 'must,' 'required,' and 'requirement,' and any other language that appears to impose substantive standards or obligations. The prohibition against making guidance statements appear binding applies to preambles as well as formal guidance documents; where a binding obligation is intended, it belongs in the regulatory text and follow APA rulemaking procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure preambles for findability and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Preambles should be written with clear structure so readers can locate preambular guidance easily, especially where rules are lengthy and preambles are long.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid writing preambles as unstructured narrative discussion. Use headings, section-by-section organization, summaries, and other structural devices. Consider electronic navigation tools (hyperlinks, anchors) to help users find guidance within long preambles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention and integrate preambles in agency guidance compilations and webpages
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should mention preambles to their final rules as sources of guidance in their general compilations of guidance and on their webpages devoted to guidance. Agencies should also consider ways to integrate the guidance content of their preambles into their general compilations of guidance and on their webpages devoted to guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make preambular guidance discoverable via the same indexes, topical treatments, and guidance libraries used for other guidance documents so the public and regulated entities can integrate preamble content with other guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance policies should address contemporaneous guidance and OMB Bulletin compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent agencies have policies on issuing guidance, those policies should assess and clearly state how they address the guidance content of preambles to their final rules. For agencies covered by OMB's Good Guidance Bulletin, their policies should address compliance with the Bulletin with respect to any significant and economically significant guidance included in preambles to final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies' internal guidance-issuance policies should explicitly include preambular guidance and state how the agency will comply with OMB requirements (e.g., public feedback mechanisms and notice-and-comment for economically significant guidance) when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide contemporaneous guidance at time of rule issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should provide contemporaneous guidance — guidance about the meaning and purpose of their rules at the time those rules are issued — to furnish the public and regulated entities with the agency's understanding of its regulations at issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contemporaneous guidance increases the legal value of notice by stating the agency's interpretation at the time of promulgation rather than later during enforcement; it can take multiple forms (preamble explanation, regulatory notes/examples, appendices, or freestanding documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use regulatory text notes, examples, and appendices as forms of contemporaneous guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies sometimes provide guidance in the regulatory text itself, in the form of notes and examples, and more general guidance in appendices that appear in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider putting clear explanatory notes and examples in the CFR where appropriate so that guidance accompanies the regulatory language; ensure such embedded guidance does not improperly create binding standards that should be in the regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop electronic CFR presentation linking to preambles and other guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of the Federal Register and the Government Printing Office are encouraged to work with agencies to develop ways to display the Code of Federal Regulations in electronic form in order to enhance its understanding and use by the public, such as developing reliable means of directing readers to relevant guidance in preambles to rules and to other relevant guidance documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic display innovations (hyperlinks from regulatory sections to relevant preambular analysis, anchors, integrated navigation) can make preambular guidance easier to find and integrate with regulatory text; agencies should experiment and adopt reliable presentation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure small entity compliance guides are easily identifiable online
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should reassess how they are displaying the small entity compliance guides on their websites to ensure that these guides are in an 'easily identified location,' as required by the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act of 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the statute requires posting such guides in easily identified locations, agencies often bury them; agencies should audit and redesign web navigation so small businesses can readily find compliance guides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Business Administration should develop posting guidelines for small entity compliance guides
rubrics_metrics.description: The Small Business Administration should work with agencies to develop guidelines for posting small entity compliance guides on agency websites in ways that make them easily identifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA-led guidelines can standardize placement, labeling, and discoverability practices across agencies to meet statutory requirements and assist small entities in locating relevant compliance information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making preamble statements that appear to create binding obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some agencies include statements in preambles to final rules that appear to create binding standards or obligations as opposed to making those statements in the regulatory text. The prohibition against agencies making statements in guidance documents in forms that appear to be binding also applies to statements in preambles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful to distinguish explanatory preambular material from binding regulatory obligations; if an obligation is intended, it should be adopted through the legislative rulemaking procedures of the APA and placed in regulatory text rather than in a preamble or guidance document.
